thread:
alex (Support): heads up — Acme is seeing 429s immediately after the rate-policy push at 09:12 PT. They report 'quota_exceeded' on /v1/generate and high client-side retries.

carrie (Customer Success): they're a paying Dedicated customer (acct: ACME_CORP). impact: several critical jobs failing, raised P1 to CS.

alex (Support): sample error from customer: 
```json
{
  "status":429,
  "error":"quota_exceeded",
  "retry_after":1
}
```
requests spiked to ~160 r/s for a 3m window — their normal is ~40 r/s with occasional 80 bursts.

maria (Eng Platform): on it — which policy ID rolled? pls paste policy id or policy name.

alex (Support): policy name: rate-v2-prod-wave1, rollout id: rb_2027_03_12_0912. We pushed a smaller burst allowance during rollout (target steady-state lower).

maria (Eng Platform): checking rollout config.. hold on.

maria (Eng Platform): quick note: I see burst_grace_seconds=0 in the new policy (should be 30). That would drop instantaneous allowance for token-bucket bursts. Could explain quick 429s for short spikes.

sam (Oncall SRE): if burst_grace_seconds got zeroed we should pause the rollout and revert to previous config. Any chance this was intentional?

maria (Eng Platform): no, the canary matrix had grace=30 but the templating job used an older fragment. Looks like a templating bug. I recommend immediate rollback of the policy fragment for wave1.

alex (Support): customer is asking for ETA, they're throttling critical pipelines.

carrie (Customer Success): Acme is amenable to a short rollback provided we confirm stability.

maria (Eng Platform): plan: 1) rollback policy fragment for rb_2027_03_12_0912 -> previous fragment with burst_grace_seconds=30 2) promote a guarded rollout (1% traffic) after fix 3) notify and keep canary paused. I'll run rollback now.

maria (Eng Platform): running: 
```bash
rdctl rollout revert --id rb_2027_03_12_0912 --target policy:rate-v2-prod-wave1 --confirm
```

deploy-bot: rollback started for rb_2027_03_12_0912 by maria (Eng Platform).

sam (Oncall SRE): observability checklist: watch 429 rate, token refill rates, per-customer counters, and latency for 30m. I'll add temporary alert suppression for noisy duplicate alerts.

maria (Eng Platform): rollback finished, new active fragment restored. Confirming: burst_grace_seconds=30, token_bucket_size restored to 200.

alex (Support): Acme retested — their spike succeeded and error rate dropped to baseline within 40s. They report retries were in-flight but cleared.

carrie (Customer Success): relayed to customer — they're relieved and want a postmortem + assurance this won't recur.

maria (Eng Platform): creating a postmortem draft and a fix for the templating path. Root cause: mismatched fragment source during canary artifact build; regression introduced by PR #987 (edge-case variable override).

sam (Oncall SRE): short-term action items: 1) add unit test for default grace value in templater 2) gate policy fragment changes with integration test that simulates short bursts 3) add a 'canary-stop-on-429' flag to automatically halt rollouts when customer-facing 429 spikes exceed threshold for 2 consecutive mins.

maria (Eng Platform): noted. I'll file follow-ups and link them here when created.

billing-bot: triggered invoice-impact calc for ACME_CORP due to service degradation window (09:12-09:22).

carrie (Customer Success): we'll coordinate credits if needed after postmortem.

alex (Support): closing loop for now — Acme confirmed systems green. Marking thread resolved but keeping postmortem thread open. :white_check_mark:
